stories.headline: Polis requests second major disaster declaration over Southwest Colorado flooding
stories.summary:
Gov. Jared Polis has asked the federal government for a second major disaster declaration after another round of historic flooding in Southwest Colorado. The request covers flooding in the region and the San Luis Valley on Oct. 31 and Nov. 1.

Polis filed a first request on Oct. 31 for flooding that struck Oct. 22-25. The governor's office said two requests were needed because they were distinct weather events. Polis said the state met the minimum damage threshold for both events under FEMA criteria, so they were filed separately even though the state manages recovery as one effort.

The governor's office said federal and state assessments have validated $28.5 million in public assistance damages from the second event. A total of 271 primary homes were destroyed or deemed uninhabitable, and another 136 homes across four counties are included in the request for individual assistance.

Polis said hundreds of families have lost homes and that roads and bridges were washed away as winter approaches. La Plata County Commissioner Matt Salka and Pagosa Springs Mayor Shari Price said federal funding is essential to rebuilding. Price said that without it, recovery would be very hard and take a very long time.

stories.headline: Denver police detective accused of drunk driving, fleeing crash in city-issued SUV
stories.summary:
A Denver police detective was accused of driving drunk, hitting a parked car and fleeing the scene in an unmarked, city-issued 2024 Chevrolet Tahoe, according to CBS Colorado. The detective was later identified as Jamie Major, a 26-year veteran of the Denver Police Department.

Residents said they heard a noise like a dumpster being dropped, and one witness said the SUV pulled away quickly after the collision. A resident who is an Army veteran followed the vehicle to help keep it from endangering other drivers. A nearby Ring camera also captured the SUV leaving the scene.

The Tahoe lost its right front tire in the crash but kept moving on the rim for about a mile. Deputies caught up with it near Yale and Monaco and stopped it at gunpoint before identifying the driver.

Major was charged with DUI and other offenses and has resigned from the department.
stories.source: The Times of India (citing CBS Colorado)

stories.headline: Rockies acquire pitchers Luis Castillo and Davis Martin from White Sox
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rockies acquired right-handers Luis Castillo and Davis Martin from the Chicago White Sox on Thursday. Colorado sent left-hander Sean Sullivan, Chicago's No. 27 prospect, and Douglas Veliz, a 17-year-old catcher from the Dominican Summer League.

Castillo, who turns 34 on Dec. 12, is a three-time All-Star who struggled after joining the White Sox at the 2026 trade deadline. He is 88-95 with a 3.75 ERA over 10 seasons. The Rockies will take on his full $24.15 million salary for 2027.

Martin, 29, went 9-8 with a 3.95 ERA last season. He becomes arbitration-eligible in 2028 and is under contractual control through 2030. He reunites with new Rockies pitching coach Ethan Katz, who held the same job in Chicago from 2021 to 2025.

Starting pitching is the club's top priority after a 58-104 season, its fourth straight with 100-plus losses. The Rockies had the majors' highest ERA at 5.59 and the highest by starters at 6.28. Kyle Freeland, Tomoyuki Sugano and Jose Quintana are exploring free agency.

stories.headline: One killed in shooting in Denver's East Colfax neighborhood
stories.summary:
One person died after being shot in Denver's East Colfax neighborhood on Thursday. Initial reports said the victim was taken to a hospital, where the person later died.

The shooting occurred Thursday, according to reporting from KDVR and the Denver Post. Further details, including the victim's identity and any suspect information, were not immediately available.

The Denver Police Department is expected to investigate. Residents with information are generally encouraged to contact police or Denver Crime Stoppers.

stories.headline: Avalanche rookie Gavin Brindley diagnosed with concussion
stories.summary:
Colorado Avalanche rookie forward Gavin Brindley has been confirmed to have a concussion. He must complete the NHL's concussion protocol before he can return to the lineup.

No timeline for his recovery has been announced. The injury adds to a growing list of Avalanche players dealing with injuries this season.

The team has several days off and will not play again until Wednesday, Nov. 25. That break gives Brindley time to progress through the protocol without missing additional games right away.

stories.headline: Colorado State Patrol urges drivers to prepare vehicles for winter weather
stories.summary:
With snow in the forecast, the Colorado State Patrol is reminding drivers to prepare their vehicles for winter conditions. Trooper Hunter Mathews said motorists driving through the mountains or in blizzards should carry shovels, food, water, snacks, blankets and things for children to do.

Mathews said the supplies can help drivers who get stuck in traffic or stranded, particularly when a tow truck or the State Patrol may be too far away to help quickly. Emergency responders will always try to assist, he said, but being prepared lets drivers help themselves while they wait.

He added that if a blizzard completely shuts down a roadway and there is no safe way to reach stranded drivers, troopers will look for the best time to get in and bring them out.

Mathews also reminded drivers about Colorado's Passenger Vehicle Traction and Chain Laws, which require passenger vehicles to have winter tires on I-70 between Morrison and Dotsero.

stories.headline: I-25 lanes south of Denver closed after hazardous materials incident near Lone Tree
stories.summary:
An on-ramp was closed and the right lanes of southbound Interstate 25 were blocked Friday morning near Lone Tree. Firefighters responded to a hazardous materials incident on the interstate.

The incident began after a fuel tank was damaged when it detached from a commercial vehicle. The closure affected part of the morning commute for drivers heading south of Denver.

Crews were working at the scene. Drivers were advised to expect delays and consider alternate routes until the roadway is cleared.

stories.headline: Denver weighs tenant protections, from right to organize to rent payment diversion
stories.summary:
Denver officials are considering new measures aimed at reining in neglectful landlords. The proposals discussed before the City Council include a right for tenants to organize and a rent payment diversion mechanism.

Tenant advocates, including the Denver Metro Tenants Union, have pushed for stronger protections. The union's executive director, Eida Altman, has previously held news conferences at properties such as the Cedar Run Apartments to highlight conditions faced by renters.

The discussions reflect ongoing concern about housing quality and the balance of power between tenants and property owners in the city. Specifics of the proposals, including timelines and any council votes, were not detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.headline: Former DIA CEO Phil Washington honored with Denver Business Journal Pinnacle Award
stories.summary:
Phillip A. Washington, the former CEO of Denver International Airport, is the winner of the Denver Business Journal's Most Admired CEO Pinnacle Award.

Washington reflected on his tenure leading the airport, one of the region's largest economic engines. He has since moved into a new role advising on infrastructure at the firm HNTB.

The recognition highlights his continued influence in the region's infrastructure and transportation sector after leaving DIA.

stories.headline: Benzina, 4.7-star Denver pizzeria on Colfax, to close Dec. 13
stories.summary:
Benzina, a pizzeria and Italian restaurant on Denver's Colfax Avenue, will close in the coming weeks, citing headwinds that were too strong, especially on Colfax. The restaurant announced the closure on Nov. 16, and its last day of service is Sunday, Dec. 13.

The restaurant has served the Denver area for five and a half years and holds a 4.7-star rating on Google Reviews. It is known for its arancini, wood-fired pizza, meatballs and smoked trout Caesar salad. Reviewers praised its made-from-scratch approach.

Until closing, Benzina will stay open an extra half-hour each night so customers can have a final meal. Restaurateur Brad Anderson thanked loyal customers in a goodbye letter, saying they tried hard to keep the doors open.

stories.headline: Colorado senators split over permitting reform package
stories.summary:
Colorado's two U.S. senators diverged over a permitting reform package that passed the Senate by a vote of 62-33.

The legislation aims to change how federal permits are approved. The split between Colorado's senators underscores differing views on the measure.

Further details on each senator's position and the contents of the package were not available in the excerpt provided by CPR News.

topStory.headline: Zelensky Calls Crimean Bridge Strikes 'Fair Response' to Russian Attacks as UK Defence Secretary Visits Kyiv
topStory.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday defended Ukraine's repeated strikes on the Crimean Bridge, calling them a "fair response" to what he said were 109 Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine. Speaking to the BBC and at a briefing in Kyiv with visiting UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, Zelensky said the strikes, carried out this week with missiles and drones, destroyed the central road section of the bridge. Part of the roadway and one of two support arches collapsed into the Kerch Strait, leaving the structure unusable for road traffic. Ukraine's Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said Ukrainian forces used domestically produced Flamingo and Neptune missiles, and that the railway section was also damaged.

Zelensky rejected Russian President Vladimir Putin's assertion that the bridge is "exclusively civilian" in use, pointing to publicly available online footage of Russian tanks, armored vehicles and artillery crossing it. "It's not secret. It's not from intelligence. It's from ordinary people," he said. He also described the heavy Russian attacks that followed the bridge strikes as a signal that Putin "does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate." Putin has vowed to respond with greater force.

In Moscow, Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said Russia has not yet determined how long repairs will take, saying designers are still calculating. He said both the steel arch and the main beam supporting the roadway were damaged, and earlier suggested that "certain elements" could reopen within one to two months, though winter storms would complicate work. Engineers cited by The New York Times said replacing the collapsed 750-foot arch could take about two years under wartime conditions, while Khmara estimated that lifting and moving the fallen section could take several months to a year. The bridge remains closed to road traffic, rail service has partially resumed on a single track, and Crimea's civilian airports remain closed to regular passenger flights. Authorities are diverting motorists to the R-280 highway through occupied southern Ukraine, which has also come under Ukrainian attack. It was the fourth time Ukraine has struck the bridge since the 2022 invasion.

Streeting said his visit was meant to show that Europe is united in its support for Ukraine, stating, "The more Putin tries to divide us, the more resolute we become." He called Russian missiles that struck Poland on Friday, during exercises of the Coalition of the Willing, an "outrageous provocation" and said the timing seemed "more than a coincidence." Asked about NATO's response, he said the best approach was to "do more for Ukraine" so it can defend itself.

The developments come amid intensifying diplomacy. European leaders meeting in Berlin on Thursday with U.S. envoys, including Jared Kushner, said they were ready for negotiations with Moscow. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Europe has a "clear and consistent and united negotiating position," and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic." Kushner said President Donald Trump, who joined by phone from Air Force One, wants a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side." The meeting followed trilateral talks in Shenzhen, China, among Putin, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Putin has so far rejected a European role in the U.S.-led talks, though he invited European representatives to Moscow to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks." Zelensky said he did not hear Trump threaten European leaders in Berlin, adding that "it is impossible to pressure Europe today."
